cells.tense: You are here with both hands on it, seeing what is actually moving between people.
cells.act: calibrate what you say to what can be heard
cells.ask: Before the next thing you say that matters, know what this person can actually take in right now. Then say it at that size — no smaller, no larger. Do it once this week.
cells.core:
You can read what's moving between people — who's carrying the meaning for a group, who's pretending to, what's actually happening under the meeting. And you're inside it, not above it, so what you say tends to land where you aimed it. That is what makes this work: your read of what connects is accurate, and you spend it on people rather than on being right about them.

The cost is that a room has many speeds. You can see the far end of a conversation while someone else is still finding the start of it, and leading with the far end is how a good read goes wrong. Calibrate what you say to what can be heard. What you get for it is the thing you're after — a connection that holds up, not one that was impressive once.
cells.sheetLine: You read the room and you're still in it.
cells.verb: Moving people toward what matters by charging into what connects
cells.place: Standing inside the system and seeing across all of its layers

cells.tense: You will already be at the ending of a conversation before anyone else has found the beginning.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Pick the one change in how people are working together that is genuinely needed. Not the whole redesign — the next real inch of it. Take that inch this week, steadily, and leave the rest alone for now.
cells.core:
You can see where this group is heading, and you're about to get there ahead of them and announce it. The pattern is real, the urgency is real, and being first to name it isn't the same as being useful. What you're braced against is the slow part, where people need to come alongside at a speed you didn't pick.

The way back runs through the small real move. Take the one inch of change that's actually needed, do it with your own hands, slowly, without announcing it. Structures that needed to fall, fall that way. The bracing loosens once the change is happening out there rather than in your head. What you get is a shift that holds without you standing over it.
cells.sheetLine: You're naming the end before anyone's found the start.
cells.verb: Moving people toward what matters by charging into what connects

cells.tense: You saw how it all fit together once, and you have not stood there since.
cells.ask: Take something you're actually in — a job, a group, a room you're part of — and quietly work out the next three moves that would make it better. Reason it out in your head, fast and clean, in one sitting. Don't do anything with it yet.
cells.core:
That way of taking in a whole situation is still in you, and it went quiet somewhere along the way. Now when you're in a group you take the surface reading and set aside whatever sits under it. Some of that is real — sometimes a room doesn't want your read. But this is running thin, thin isn't gone, and the fastest way back isn't to feel your way into it.

It's to think. Work the logic of something you're in, quick and clean, all the way to its sharp point, the way you used to. You don't have to act on it or say it. Thinking a thing through precisely opens the eye that takes in the whole of it. What you get is the pattern again, arriving through the front door this time instead of by accident.
cells.sheetLine: That eye is still in you. It just went quiet.
cells.verb: Moving people toward what matters by charging into what connects
cells.place: Standing inside the system and seeing across all of its layers

cells.tense: You are holding the shape of this group and calling it nothing in particular.
cells.act: say the hard thing gently, once
cells.ask: There's something you've noticed that you keep not saying, because it would land awkwardly or because nobody asked. Say it. Once, gently, to the person it concerns. Then leave it and don't bring it up again.
cells.core:
You are the person who keeps the meaning in this group steady — you know the tone of it, you know what people actually mean, you adjust what you say so it keeps working. Asked to describe it, you'd say the group has its own way, or that you're just paying attention. Nobody has ever called it a skill, so it doesn't feel like one.

The next time you notice something true and quietly decide it isn't worth raising, raise it — calibrated, once, to the person it concerns. Then let it be. A thing said at full size doesn't need a follow-up. What you get is knowing this craft is yours, rather than finding out later that the room seemed to run itself without help.
cells.sheetLine: Keeping this group working is something you're doing.
cells.verb: Moving people toward what matters by charging into what connects
cells.place: Standing inside the system and seeing across all of its layers

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person is the one who charges toward connection and creates change through emotional intensity — the draw shows a capacity for that, not proof it is running anywhere in their life. A reader could reasonably say they are not the catalyst type at all, and the ask would still stand: noticing what they truly want to say before speaking is useful to anyone. The sentence that serves me more than them is 'You see the whole pattern,' which flatters the seat and tells them nothing they can use; I will not put it on glass in those words.
